correctness.rationale: For nonnegative data, exact star-ball averages yield F_i(g)=max(g_i,g_i/2,μ)-max(0,μ), μ=Σ g_j/(m+1), with any gradient g realized by positive baseline. Across all piecewise-affine cells, each weighted ℓ1 column sum is bounded by w_j+(W-w_j)/(m+1). Explicit positive inputs with μ<0, one high leaf and all others at g_i=-1 attain equality. The two-vertex case is F_1(g)=g/2. A constant signed shift gives zero input variation but nonzero output-difference variation. Exact checker passed 127926 formal selector columns, 20 attaining pairs, 5000 random rational secants and seven signed counterexample instances; finite tests support but do not replace the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected star-graph maximal operator results concern one-input weighted or unweighted mapping inequalities. In particular, the published one-input sharp variation ratio m/(m+1) for m leaves is not a two-input Lipschitz inequality for the nonlinear difference Mf-Mh. The new exact independent-weight two-input ratio 1+(W-wmin)/((m+1)wmin), equal-weight twofold separation, strictly positive attaining pairs, and unique optimal weighting are not implied by the inspected results or closest accessible mathematical records. Residual risk of an implicit prior formulation is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The star and centered maximal graph averaging are canonical. The exact sharp two-data variation modulus addresses perturbation stability, rather than the known single-signal regularity bound. It shows every genuine star is expansive, uniform edge weights uniquely minimize amplification, sensitivity diverges under vanishing weight, and the cone restriction is mathematically necessary. The doubled uniform-weight factor is an interpretable and motivated invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
